transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?
I’ve been planning my days around avoiding high bridges. If I can’t avoid one, I get through it, but I’m gripping the wheel the whole time—just white-knuckling it.
Aside from bridges, do you have similar intense fear or avoidance in other situations, like being in crowds, open spaces, or far from home?
No, I haven’t really noticed that in other situations. It’s mainly the high bridges.
How long have you been experiencing this fear of high bridges—weeks, months, or longer?
About two years now. It started after I moved out during my separation and was driving around the county more.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent, marked fear specifically triggered by high bridges, present for about two years, leading to active avoidance or endurance with significant anxiety (white-knuckling while driving). The fear is confined to this specific situational trigger without generalization to other agoraphobic-type situations (crowds, open spaces, being away from home), ruling out agoraphobia (F40.00). There is no mention of pervasive, free-floating worry across multiple domains as seen in generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1). The circumscribed nature of the fear, its situational specificity (high places/bridges), duration exceeding 6 months, and associated avoidance behavior meet criteria for specific phobia, other type (fear of heights/high bridges), coded as F40.218.
